data.title: Insufficient Network Segmentation
data.summary: The internal network was substantially flat: hosts in user subnets could reach servers, management interfaces and other users' machines without restriction. A foothold anywhere therefore provided reach everywhere.
data.description:
Segmentation decides what a compromise costs. In a flat network, one phished workstation reaches domain controllers, databases, backup systems, hypervisors and every other workstation — so the first foothold is effectively the last obstacle.

Lateral movement in that environment is indistinguishable from normal traffic, because normal traffic goes everywhere too. There is no boundary at which a request from a workstation to a backup server looks wrong.

Workstation-to-workstation traffic deserves particular attention: it is rarely needed, and it is the path used for both lateral movement and ransomware propagation.
data.recommendation:
* Segment by function and sensitivity — users, servers, management, OT, guest — and filter between segments by default-deny.
* Block workstation-to-workstation traffic except where a business case requires it.
* Place management interfaces in a dedicated segment reachable only through a bastion.
* Verify segmentation by testing from each segment rather than by reading the intended design.
data.short_recommendation: Segment by function and filter between segments by default.
